### P0010. Biased random square-lattice orientations

**Source.** Selected problems in probability theory (grimmett_2022_selected), Question 5.1, PDF page 9.

**Statement.** Does every nonzero orientation bias give positive probability of an infinite directed path from the origin?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Directed-percolation subgraph comparison. Result: Reflecting both coordinate axes maps p to 1-p, so the infinite-path probability is symmetric about one-half. North-east paths use independent edges pointing north/east with probability p; survival of the usual north-east directed percolation therefore implies survival in the full oriented graph. The p=0 and p=1 endpoints have deterministic infinite paths.. Obstruction: It does not settle the interval between one-half and that threshold. The critical p=1/2 result does not extend by continuity alone.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0011. Brownian SIR survival in dimensions at least two

**Source.** Selected problems in probability theory (grimmett_2022_selected), Question 6.1(ii), PDF pages 9-10.

**Statement.** Does the fully diffusing Poisson Brownian SIR model survive for sufficiently small positive removal rate when d>=2?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Counterexample to the usual pathwise lifetime monotonicity coupling. Result: Consider a deterministic contact schedule with A initially infected: A-C at time .1, A-B at 1, C-B at 9, B-D at 10, and no other contacts. Baseline infectious lifetimes are L_A=.5, L_C=12, L_B=2. Then B is infected at 9 and infects D at 10. Multiply every lifetime by 3: A now infects B at 1; B is removed at 7, cannot be reinfected at 9, and D is never infected.. Obstruction: This is not a counterexample to survival monotonicity or to the Brownian epidemic conjecture. It blocks a direct attractiveness proof; a Brownian contact-support realization was not proved.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0012. Gaussian tensor type-2 bound

**Source.** Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025 (randomstrasse_2025_v1), Conjecture 16, Entry 8.

**Statement.** For symmetric order-r tensors T_i on R^d, p>=2 and independent standard Gaussians g_i, is E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) bounded by polylog(d,n) times O_(r,p)(d^(1/2-1/p) sqrt(sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2))?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Diagonal-tensor Gaussian estimate. Result: For a diagonal homogeneous form T(x)=sum_j a_j x_j^r and 2<=p<=r, its supremum over the l_p unit ball is max_j |a_j|. Indeed sum |x_j|^r<=1 and a coordinate vector attains the maximum. For independent standard g_i, each diagonal coefficient of sum_i g_i T_i has variance at most sum_i ||T_i||^2, so the Gaussian maximum bound gives E||sum_i g_i T_i|| <= sqrt(2 log(2d)) (sum_i ||T_i||^2)^(1/2).. Obstruction: This verifies a restricted diagonal family. Off-diagonal terms and the full p range require the tensor geometry absent here.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0013. Expected Lovasz theta of a dense independent-edge graph

**Source.** Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025 (randomstrasse_2025_v1), Conjecture 17, Entry 9.

**Statement.** For G distributed as G(n,1/2), is E theta(G)=(1+o(1)) sqrt(n)?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Complement symmetry and uniform-integrability obstruction. Result: The theta product inequality theta(G) theta(complement G)>=n and complement symmetry of G(n,1/2) give E theta>=sqrt(n) by arithmetic-geometric mean. A proof of concentration on a logarithmic scale would still need tail control: set Z_n to plus or minus (log n)/2, each with probability 1/(2 sqrt(n)), and zero otherwise. Then Z_n tends to zero in probability and variance, but E exp(Z_n) tends to 3/2.. Obstruction: Need a sharp upper bound and uniform integrability at the sqrt(n) scale; complement symmetry only yields the lower bound.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0014. Expected Lovasz theta of a random circulant graph

**Source.** Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025 (randomstrasse_2025_v1), Conjecture 18, Entry 9.

**Statement.** For the graph on Z/nZ formed by independently including each unordered nonzero generator pair {k,-k} with probability 1/2, is E theta(G)=(1+o(1)) sqrt(n)?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Vertex-transitive complement identity. Result: A circulant graph is vertex transitive, so theta(G) theta(complement G)=n. Its random model is complement invariant. For Z=log(theta(G)/sqrt(n)), Z has the law of -Z and E theta/sqrt(n)=E cosh Z. The conjecture is therefore equivalent to E(cosh Z-1) tending to zero.. Obstruction: Must estimate the exponential tails of the logarithmic theta fluctuation for the dependent circulant adjacency structure.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0015. Random complex phase-retrieval injectivity at 4M-5 measurements

**Source.** Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025 (randomstrasse_2025_v1), Conjecture 19(a,b), Entry 10.

**Statement.** Let p_M be the probability that a complex Gaussian (4M-5)-by-M matrix gives an injective phaseless measurement map modulo global phase. Is p_M<1 for each meaningful M, and does p_M tend to zero?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Complete M=2 obstruction via Hermitian lifting. Result: For M=2 the matrix has three complex Gaussian rows. Almost surely these span C^2. The real-linear measurement map from the four-dimensional Hermitian 2-by-2 space to R^3 has a nonzero kernel element H. H cannot be positive or negative semidefinite: a_i^* H a_i=0 for a spanning set would force H=0. Thus H has one positive and one negative eigenvalue and can be written xx^*-yy^* with noncollinear x,y. Their three intensity measurements agree. Hence p_2=0.. Obstruction: For M>2 a nonzero kernel matrix need not have rank at most two with one eigenvalue of each sign. The requisite low-rank intersection probability remains unresolved.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0016. Worst square-submatrix conditioning in a Gaussian frame

**Source.** Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025 (randomstrasse_2025_v1), Open Problem 21 and Definition 10.1, Entry 10.

**Statement.** For a (2M-1)-by-M matrix of independent standard real Gaussians, determine the asymptotic size of omega(A), the minimum smallest singular value over row subsets whose complement has rank below M. In particular determine whether its decay is exponential and identify the exponential rate.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Union small-ball lower bound and one-normal upper bound. Result: For a standard M-by-M real Gaussian matrix A, sigma_min(A)<=t implies that some column has distance at most sqrt(M)t from the span of the other columns: project a minimizing unit vector equation using a coordinate of magnitude at least 1/sqrt(M). Each such distance has the law |N(0,1)|, so P(sigma_min<=t)<=sqrt(2/pi) M^(3/2)t. There are at most 4^M M-row submatrices of a (2M-1)-by-M frame. Therefore its minimum omega exceeds exp(-(log 4+epsilon)M) with probability tending to one. Conversely fix M-1 rows and a unit normal u. The M remaining row projections are independent N(0,1), and omega is at most their minimum absolute value, giving omega<=C log(M)/M with probability tending to one for sufficiently large C.. Obstruction: The exponential lower bound and polynomial upper bound are far apart. Sharp extremes of the strongly dependent minors remain uncontrolled.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0017. Dimension-free log-concave Poincare or Cheeger constant

**Source.** Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025 (randomstrasse_2025_v1), Conjecture 30, Entry 13.

**Statement.** Is there a universal positive lower bound for the Euclidean Cheeger constant of every isotropic log-concave probability measure, in every dimension?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Gaussian special case by orthogonal expansion. Result: For standard Gaussian measure, expand a polynomial f in orthonormal multivariate Hermite polynomials with coefficients a_alpha. Then Var(f)=sum_(|alpha|>=1) a_alpha^2 <= sum |alpha| a_alpha^2 = E||gradient f||^2. Closure in Gaussian Sobolev norm extends the inequality to its natural domain.. Obstruction: A general isotropic log-concave measure lacks this diagonal Hermite generator. This special case does not prove its uniform Poincare or Cheeger bound.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0018. Sharp polynomial-logarithmic expected norm of graph matrices

**Source.** Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025 (randomstrasse_2025_v1), Conjecture 31 and Definition 14.2, Entry 14.

**Statement.** For each fixed graph shape alpha with specified left and right index sets, form M_alpha by summing injective labelings with products of independent Rademacher edge variables. Must E||M_alpha|| be Theta(n^f(alpha) (log n)^g(alpha)) for some shape-dependent exponents?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Moment expansion with a crude operator-norm bound. Result: For every finite random graph matrix, E||M|| <= (E||M||_F^2)^(1/2). Expanding each entry as a sum of Rademacher edge monomials, cross terms vanish unless the two monomials use every edge with even combined multiplicity. For a fixed shape the remaining label identifications can be counted to obtain a polynomial upper bound in n.. Obstruction: The Frobenius bound can lose powers of n and cannot decide the sharp operator norm or the existence of one power-log asymptotic form.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0019. Brownian exit approach directions in higher dimensions

**Source.** Krzysztof Burdzy: My favorite open problems (burdzy_open_20260906), Problem 1.

**Statement.** For Brownian motion exiting a domain in dimension d>2, is the set of limiting approach directions at the exit point almost surely a sphere or a hemisphere?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Smooth-boundary directional containment. Result: At an exit point z where the domain boundary is C^1 with outward unit normal n, local differentiability gives n dot (z-x)>=-o(|z-x|) for x in the domain approaching z. Thus every limit of (z-B_s)/|z-B_s| as s increases to the exit time lies in the closed hemisphere {u:n dot u>=0}.. Obstruction: Containment does not prove that all hemisphere directions occur, and there is no supporting tangent half-space at the arbitrary boundaries in the full question.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0020. Finite-crossing arcs through a planar Brownian trace

**Source.** Krzysztof Burdzy: My favorite open problems (burdzy_open_20260906), Problem 2(i).

**Statement.** Almost surely, can every two points outside the trace of planar Brownian motion on [0,1] be connected by a Jordan arc meeting the trace at only finitely many points?

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Reduction to component adjacency and access. Result: If both endpoints lie in the same component of the complement of the Brownian trace, an open connected planar set is polygonally connected; removing loops gives a simple arc avoiding the trace entirely. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0147. Fluctuations of weighted flooding and diameter on configuration models

**Source.** Van der Hofstad: Stochastic processes on random graphs, Saint-Flour2017 (rhofstad_saintflour_2017), Open Problem3.5, PDF pp.150-151.

**Statement.** Identify centered fluctuation laws for exponential-weight flooding time and weighted diameter in the configuration-model regimes of Theorem3.37.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Fluctuations of weighted flooding and diameter on configuration models structural reduction. Result: On any fixed graph, the minimum incident exponential edge weight at a degree-d vertex is Exp(d). For a collection of m pairwise nonadjacent degree-d vertices these minima use disjoint edge sets and are independent. Hence P(d max X_v-log m<=x)=(1-exp(-x)/m)^m tends to exp(-exp(-x)).. Obstruction: This identifies one endpoint-delay component of the extremes. The bulk connecting distances and their dependence on the extreme endpoints are not controlled, so no full flooding or diameter limit is claimed.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0148. General edge-weight laws for random-graph flooding and diameter

**Source.** Van der Hofstad: Stochastic processes on random graphs, Saint-Flour2017 (rhofstad_saintflour_2017), Open Problem3.6, PDF p.152.

**Statement.** Extend weighted flooding-time and diameter asymptotics from exponential weights to general iid nonnegative edge-weight laws on the configuration model.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: General edge-weight laws for random-graph flooding and diameter structural reduction. Result: At a degree-d vertex the minimum incident weight X has tail P(X>t)=(1-F(t))^d. Over m nonadjacent such vertices, P(max X_v<=t)=[1-(1-F(t))^d]^m. For weights E^s this gives max X_v asymptotic to(log m/d)^s in probability.. Obstruction: Endpoint delays alone can change scale, but the fastest route through the bulk is a different optimization. Matching these two mechanisms for general F is still missing.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0149. Extreme hopcounts for general random-graph degree and weight laws

**Source.** Van der Hofstad: Stochastic processes on random graphs, Saint-Flour2017 (rhofstad_saintflour_2017), Open Problem3.7, PDF p.152.

**Statement.** Determine the first-order extreme hopcount from one root and over all pairs for general configuration-model degree laws, and extend beyond exponential edge weights.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Extreme hopcounts for general random-graph degree and weight laws structural reduction. Result: On a graph with maximum degree Delta, there are at most n*Delta*(Delta-1)^(k-1) oriented simple k-edge paths. With iid weights Y, the chance any such path has total weight at most t is at most this count times exp(a*t)*(E exp(-aY))^k for every a>0.. Obstruction: The bound is too crude when a few hubs make Delta large and does not automatically constrain minimizing paths with unknown total cost. Degree-biased branching and extreme endpoint selection require sharper control.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0150. Minimal assumptions for heavy-tailed critical metric convergence

**Source.** Van der Hofstad: Stochastic processes on random graphs, Saint-Flour2017 (rhofstad_saintflour_2017), Open Problem4.2, PDF p.218; Theorem4.39.

**Statement.** Remove the extra degree restrictions used to upgrade heavy-tailed critical configuration-model components from Gromov-weak convergence to Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov convergence.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record.). Admission: admitted; result_status: attempted_unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Minimal assumptions for heavy-tailed critical metric convergence structural reduction. Result: Let X_n=[0,1] with the ordinary metric and probability measure(1-1/n)delta_0+(1/n)Lebesgue. Every fixed finite iid sample from this measure lies at0 with probability tending to1, so its distance matrices converge to those of a point. Yet the spaces all have diameter1 and cannot converge in Gromov-Hausdorff distance to a point.. Obstruction: This is a precise failure of weak measured convergence to control thin appendages. A uniform lower bound on masses of fixed-radius balls is the missing type of estimate.. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument. No proof file recorded.


## Catalog: Codex 1,000-open-problems campaign (Probability_1000_20h_20260906), P0151-P0300

This chapter covers 150 problem rows, P0151 through P0300, from the Codex campaign ledger at ~/Downloads/Probability_1000_20h_20260906 (problems.jsonl, attempts.jsonl, sources.jsonl, README.md, STATUS.json, RESUME.md; no separate CORRECTIONS.md file exists in this campaign directory, and problems.jsonl and attempts.jsonl are themselves append-only ledgers, so a row's current state is its last-recorded version, and any prior version it supersedes is reported below entry by entry). Of the 150 rows, 135 are admitted as distinct open questions and 15 are not admitted, all 15 of them because a later status search or attempt found the question already resolved in the literature (result_status excluded_prior_resolution). Result-status counts across the shard: attempted_unsolved: 94, candidate_full_solution: 9, candidate_partial_counterexample: 1, excluded_prior_resolution: 15, partial_counterexample_author_checked: 1, unsolved: 30. 12 rows carry a written proof or counterexample memo under proofs/ (referenced by problem_id below). 8 rows in this range were corrected mid-campaign by a later record in the same append-only problems.jsonl file (two are exclusions superseding an earlier candidate-solution status, citing a named prior-literature resolution; the rest are result_status relabelings or metadata date corrections), and each such row names the correcting record in its entry. Every attempt in this shard is author-checked at most; the ledger records zero independently reviewed or independently certified original solutions in this range, and this report makes no claim of publishable novelty for any of it.

### P0151. Critical window for fixed-outdegree preferential attachment

Source: rhofstad_saintflour_2017, Open Problem4.4, PDF p.220. Statement: For affine preferential attachment with a fixed m>=2 edges per arriving vertex and delta>0, identify the percolation scaling window and largest critical component sizes. (The percolation threshold itself is covered by later work2312.14085. The2025 growing-graph window theorem concerns models with independently attached edges; it is not automatically the fixed-outdegree model asked here.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Critical window for fixed-outdegree preferential attachment structural reduction. Local weak convergence alone cannot determine macroscopic cluster sizes. A single cycle on n vertices and a disjoint union of cycles whose lengths are about sqrt(n) have the same local weak limit, the two-sided infinite path, but their largest components have orders n and sqrt(n). Obstruction: This prevents deriving the critical window from the Polya-point local limit alone. A growing-scale exploration argument must retain age and fixed-outdegree dependencies. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument.

### P0152. Kernel criteria for critical inhomogeneous random-graph universality

Source: rhofstad_saintflour_2017, Open Problem4.5-4.6, PDF pp.222-223. Statement: Characterize critical component universality for general inhomogeneous random-graph kernels, including the proposed role of the positive principal eigenfunction belonging to L3. (The general question and the eigenfunction criterion are grouped. Rank-one and finite-type theorems do not cover every irreducible unbounded kernel.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Kernel criteria for critical inhomogeneous random-graph universality structural reduction. L3 integrability of the principal eigenfunction does not itself give a spectral gap. Partition[0,1] into blocks of masses p_i tending to0, choose epsilon_i>0 tending to0, and let m=sum p_i epsilon_i. On blocks i,j set kappa=(1-epsilon_i)1{i=j}/p_i+epsilon_i epsilon_j/m. Obstruction: The example is an obstruction to using an unstated spectral-gap consequence of the conjectured criterion. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument.

### P0153. Vacant-set percolation threshold on general configuration models

Source: rhofstad_saintflour_2017, Open Problem4.8, PDF p.225. Statement: Identify the critical time for percolation of the vacant set left after a random walk runs for order n time on a configuration model, including degree laws with diverging second moment. (Time normalization, the giant component, and initial distribution must match the source. The suggestion that the threshold vanishes for infinite second moment is a question, not an established consequence of ordinary percolation.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Vacant-set percolation threshold on general configuration models structural reduction. For simple random walk on a finite connected graph, stationary mass at v is d_v/sum_w d_w. This controls expected occupation counts in stationarity, but it does not identify the probability of ever visiting v: repeated returns can account for many occupation times. Obstruction: Degree-biased occupation cannot be substituted for independent vertex deletion. One needs escape probabilities and joint avoidance estimates to determine the critical remaining branching structure. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument.

Source: rhofstad_saintflour_2017, Open Problem4.9, PDF p.225. Statement: Obtain metric-space scaling limits for the largest critical vacant-set components of general configuration models, including heavy-tailed degree sequences. (Random-regular vacant-set metric limits are already established. The general degree law and possible suppression of high-degree hubs form the unresolved extension.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Metric scaling of critical random-walk vacant components structural reduction. A high degree need not imply large escape capacity. Attach K leaves to a vertex v that has just one additional edge leading into a fixed transient infinite tree. Obstruction: The example is not a configuration-model limit theorem. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument.

(Correct window centering and constants are part of the source question. Results for a growing-dimensional hypercube, or order-of-magnitude estimates, are not automatically this fixed-d torus theorem.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Erdos-Renyi component-size limits for high-dimensional tori structural reduction. Two-sided order bounds cannot identify a scaling law: random variables X_n=n^(2/3)A_n, where A_n alternates between two different bounded positive distributions, always have the predicted magnitude and are tight after scaling, but have different subsequential limits. Source: rhofstad_saintflour_2017, Open Problem4.11-4.12, PDF p.231. Statement: Identify and prove the metric-measure scaling limits of minimum spanning trees on configuration models with minimum limiting degree at least3, across finite-third-moment and heavy-tailed degree regimes. (The two source regimes are grouped. The random3-regular case is resolved by Addario-Berry and Sen1810.03802; it is excluded from the open remainder. The law of iid continuous edge weights is not an extra family of distinct problems.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Configuration-model minimum spanning-tree metric limits structural reduction. For a fixed finite graph with distinct edge weights, applying any strictly increasing function to every weight leaves the minimum spanning tree unchanged. Kruskal's algorithm inspects edges in the same order and makes the same cycle decisions. Obstruction: The remaining difficulty is the graph ensemble and the global near-critical component-merger geometry. Rank invariance does not establish tightness, scaling exponents, or the limiting tree. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument.

(The asymptotic regime must have epsilon_n tending to0 with n epsilon_n^3 large; otherwise the displayed logarithm is not the intended barely-subcritical scale. Infinite-third-moment results are a different regime.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Two competing largest-component scales in barely subcritical configuration models structural reduction. A branching-process approximation already explains the high-degree candidate scale. If the root has d children and every later vertex has mean offspring1-epsilon, then expected total progeny is1+d/epsilon: each child starts a subcritical tree of expected size1/epsilon. Obstruction: Expectation at a high-degree root is not a high-probability largest-component estimate. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument.

### P0158. Ordered-phase susceptibility exponent on random trees and graphs

Source: rhofstad_saintflour_2017, Open Problem5.1, PDF pp.286-287. Statement: Prove that the susceptibility critical exponent gamma_prime on the ordered side of the locally tree-like ferromagnetic Ising transition equals1 under the source's degree assumptions. (The high-temperature exponent gamma=1 and the random-regular ordered-phase case are already known. The source seeks the missing upper bound for general degree laws with a nontrivial finite critical inverse temperature.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Ordered-phase susceptibility exponent on random trees and graphs structural reduction. At zero cavity field, the expected generation-k contribution to susceptibility is proportional to nu^(k-1)*(tanh beta)^k, yielding a geometric series only when nu*tanh beta<1. Above criticality that same bound diverges, so it cannot prove the desired finite susceptibility asymptotic in the plus state. Obstruction: A sharp lower bound on that attenuation, averaged along the size-biased spine and uniformly near criticality, is missing. Verification: author_checked_limited_argument.

Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Quenched non-Gaussian critical spin limits on heterogeneous random graphs structural reduction. For environment G and partition functions Z_G(h), the averaged quenched moment generating function is E[Z_G(h)/Z_G(0)], whereas the annealed one is E Z_G(h)/E Z_G(0). These are generally different. If two equally likely environments have(Z0,Zh)=(1,1) and(2,2*cosh h), the expressions are(1+cosh h)/2 and(1+2*cosh h)/3. ### P0268. Abstract stochastic maximal regularity with non-small multiplicative noise

Source: agresti_veraar_spde_2025, Problem1,PDF91. Statement: Find abstract operator conditions yielding stochastic maximal Lp regularity for (A,B), beyond the small-B perturbation theorem. (The source asks for a satisfactory structural criterion, rather than any sufficient condition: the small-norm sufficient condition is already established.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction. For simultaneously diagonal A and B on a Hilbert space, the homogeneous coordinate equation dX=-lambda*X dt+b*sqrt(lambda)*X dW gives E|X_t|^p=|X_0|^p exp{p*((p-1)*b^2/2-1)*lambda*t}. Thus positivity of A alone cannot supply a p-independent stochastic parabolicity condition. Obstruction: A criterion handling noncommuting A,B in Banach spaces must replace scalar coercivity and preserve the correct p-dependence. No such general criterion is proved here. Verification: author_checked_partial.

### P0269. Necessary and sufficient operator criterion for stochastic maximal regularity

Source: agresti_veraar_spde_2025, Problem2,PDF92. Statement: For a sectorial operator A of angle below pi/2 on Lq, q>2, characterize stochastic maximal Lp regularity of (A,0). (A bounded H-infinity calculus is an established sufficient condition. Repeating that condition is not a solution of the necessary-and-sufficient problem.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction. In the positive diagonal Hilbert model u_k(t)=integral_0^t exp[-lambda_k*(t-s)]g_k(s)dW_s, Ito isometry and Tonelli give E integral_0^T sum_k lambda_k^2 |u_k(t)|^2 dt <= (1/2) E integral_0^T sum_k lambda_k |g_k(s)|^2 ds. The exact kernel integral is lambda_k*(1-exp[-2lambda_k*(T-s)])/2. This isolates the quadratic square-function estimate behind the property. Obstruction: For q>2, the spatial Lq norm lies outside the quadratic sum and the Hilbert Fubini computation no longer identifies the necessary operator square-function property. Verification: author_checked_partial.

### P0279. Cutoff for bounded-degree Ising throughout the rapid-mixing phase

Source: salez_markov_2025, Problem2.8,PDF31. ### P0280. Cutoff for bounded-degree hardcore throughout the rapid-mixing phase

Source: salez_markov_2025, Problem2.9,PDF32. Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction. For an edgeless graph and fixed fugacity zeta>0, the stationary coordinates are independent Bernoulli(p), p=zeta/(1+zeta). Under rate-one refreshes and initial all ones, q_t=p+(1-p)*e^-t. A one-coordinate chi-square calculation gives (q_t-p)^2/[p*(1-p)] and hence full chi-square distance [1+((1-p)/p)*e^-2t]^N-1. ### P0281. Log concavity of finite particle TASEP transition probabilities

Source: aim_kpz_2025, Section3,PDF2;follow-up Q2,PDF3. Statement: For continuous-time TASEP with n particles started from the step configuration, determine whether its fixed-time transition mass function on ordered particle configurations is log concave. (The lattice midpoint assertion is considered when the midpoint is integral and is a legal ordered configuration. A real-variable extension or a stronger rounded-midpoint notion would require a separate definition.) Status: historical status source_says_open; current status unverified. Our work: Exact identities, finite controls and structural obstruction. For one particle the displacement has Poisson mass p_k=e^-t*t^k/k!, so p_k^2/(p_(k-1)*p_(k+1))=(k+1)/k for k>=1. Thus the scalar nearest-neighbor log-concavity inequality holds strictly. Independent freely moving particles would give a product of these masses and preserve this inequality on every integral coordinate midpoint. Obstruction: Blocking changes holding rates according to the configuration. The determinantal transition formula contains signed terms, and log concavity is not preserved under signed summation. Verification: author_checked_partial.

### P0301. Full probabilistic noncompact imaginary Liouville theory

**Source.** Rhodes-Vargas: Two decades of probabilistic approach to Liouville conformal field theory,2025 (lcft_rhodes_vargas_2025), Section9,PDF18;Usciati et al2505.09390,PDF3-4.

**Statement.** Complete the probabilistic construction and identification of noncompact imaginary Liouville theory in the general non-neutral regime described by the survey. Ledger caveat: Usciati-Guillarmou-Rhodes-Santachiara give a proposed construction and exact circle results; their sphere construction depends on conjectured imaginary-chaos Laplace asymptotics. Chatterjee2504.02348 proves timelike results under charge neutrality. These partial results must not be erased or counted as new.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record recorded in the ledger). Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Explicit calculation or obstruction with source-specific scope. Result: The circle contour calculation shows why simply integrating the constant mode over a real period imposes neutrality. For an integer screening expansion, the integral of exp(i*k*beta*c) over a full period vanishes unless k=0. A noncompact complex Hankel-type contour can avoid that selection rule, but requires a large-argument estimate for the complex GMC Laplace transform along its two infinite legs. Finite exponential moments only ensure finiteness for each fixed argument, not decay along those legs. Obstruction: The missing sphere Laplace estimate and identification with the imaginary DOZZ expression remain unresolved in the read source. Current status requires later papers beyond the read2025 proposal and April2026 charge-neutral result; it is not certified open solely from the survey. Verification: author_checked_partial. No proof file recorded.

### P0302. One critically loaded queue under general k-limited polling inputs

**Source.** Boon and Winands: Open problems for critically loaded k-limited polling systems (2022) (queues_klimited_uva_2022), Conjecture1 and Problem1,journal282,PDF3.

**Statement.** Prove the general finite-variance renewal-input heavy-traffic joint limit in Boon-Winands Conjecture1: one critically loaded queue has the stated scaled exponential limit, the other converges to the stated vacation queue, and the components become independent. Ledger caveat: The exponential and phase-type special cases are already established. The source regime lambda1/k1<lambda2/k2 and scaling with fixed interarrival coefficient of variation are essential.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record recorded in the ledger). Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Explicit calculation or obstruction with source-specific scope. Result: The source switch-over variance absorption has a useful exact batch check. When the critical queue serves exactly k2 jobs per cycle, its batch time is sum of k2 iid B2 variables plus the total switch-over S. The batch variance divided by k2 is Var(B2)+Var(S)/k2. Assigning the same S/k2 to every effective job instead would give marginal variance Var(B2)+Var(S)/k2^2 but introduce correlations between those jobs. Ignoring those correlations would produce the wrong diffusion coefficient. Obstruction: This verifies the proposed effective mean and variance but not the joint stationary limit. General renewal residual lives, the stable-queue vacation environment, asymptotic independence and stationary interchange still need a proof. The source simulation correlation near zero is not a proof of independence. Verification: author_checked_partial. No proof file recorded.

Result: The no-switch-over comparison has an exact simplification: if all jobs require deterministic time2 and arrivals are the superposition of independent Poisson streams, total workload is the workload of a work-conserving M/D/1 queue, independently of the polling order. Empty visits then consume capacity, and their boundary frequencies enter the two-dimensional reflected limit. ### P0307. Exact dimension of the LQG metric net

**Source.** Bhatia Gwynne Harper: Dimension lower bounds in random geometry via Lipschitz functions (2026) (lqg_lipschitz_2026), IntroductionPDF3;discussionPDF6 afterTheorem1.3.

**Statement.** Determine the Hausdorff dimension of the LQG metric net; in particular establish the expected metric dimension3 in the Brownian-map case. Ledger caveat: One metric-net dimension family is counted. Dimensions of geodesic stars and of intersections of two nets are different targets. The2026 source lower bounds are not claimed as new.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (no status-search record recorded in the ledger). Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Explicit calculation or obstruction with source-specific scope. Result: A fixed metric sphere and the union of spheres over all radii have different dimension behavior. In the Euclidean plane, each circle about the origin has Hausdorff dimension1 while their union over radii in[1,2] is an annulus of dimension2. Its asymptotic covariance, when the joint CLT holds, is J*Sigma*J^T, where J is the Jacobian of this inversion and Sigma=sum over integer lags of Cov((1{W_0>0},W_0),(1{W_l>0},W_l)). Under its stationary Palm law, rerooting at a uniformly selected neighbor preserves the marked-vertex marginal by mass transport: send f of the receiving marked vertex along every directed edge with weight 1/(d+1). Outgoing expectation is the neighbor average and incoming mass is f at the root. Thus the separation mark of a uniformly chosen neighbor also has the source Gamma(d+1) marginal. Obstruction: Marginal preservation does not determine dependence between neighboring separation marks, lengths or angles. A joint Palm/Mecke calculation remains missing. Result: For an absolutely continuous size law with hazard h, a job at attained service a allocated b servers completes at instantaneous rate h(a)*s(b), while its age advances at rate s(b). A formal controlled generator therefore has both an age-drift term s(b)*partial_a V and a completion term h(a)*s(b)*(V_after_departure-V). Maximizing the departure rate alone drops the learning and continuation terms. The common exponential case removes age learning but does not justify that omission for a general size law. Thus the offline allocation can persist only if the stochastic value gradients preserve the required ratios; arrivals explicitly couple all coordinates through the appended-state term. Obstruction: The value gradients, boundary conditions at completion, recurrence assumptions and optimality verification remain unknown. Verification: author_checked_partial. No proof file recorded.

Allocate b to class one and 4-b to class two until the first completion, then all four to the survivor. Expected sum of completion times is V(b)=[2+s1(b)/(2*sqrt(2))+s2(4-b)/2]/[s1(b)+s2(4-b)]. The throughput maximizer is b=1: total rate increases below one and decreases above it. Yet V(81/64)<V(1). The slower departure rate improves the continuation state. ### P0429. Largest growing fork-join batch compatible with asymptotic independence

**Source.** Harchol-Balter: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing (queues_computing_frontiers_2021), Section5; PDF16.

**Statement.** Determine how quickly the number k(n) of tasks per uniformly routed job can grow while the corresponding k(n) stationary queues remain asymptotically independent. Ledger caveat: The source credits k=o(n^(1/4)); fixed-dimensional convergence alone does not answer the growing-dimensional question. Private author-only packet extends the credited coupling under exponential service. Later primary-source leads do not establish novelty.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (Focused later-primary-source checks on 2026-09-07; offline concave scheduling, general FCFS threshold representation, SEK-SMOD and fork-join asymptotics credited. No present-openness certification.). Admission: admitted; result_status: candidate_partial_counterexample. This row was revised 2 times in problems.jsonl; the latest occurrence is reported here.

**Our work.** Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison. Result: A finite-horizon input coupling suggests a cubic collision scale. Fix k tagged servers. Jobs arrive at rate Lambda=lambda*n/k and choose a uniform k-subset. If N is the number of tagged servers hit by an arrival, E[N(N-1)]=k*(k-1)*k*(k-1)/(n*(n-1)). Remove arrivals that hit at least two tagged queues and restore their lost marginal rates by independent Poisson streams. A union bound on removed events and added events is at most (3/2)*Lambda*T*E[N(N-1)], hence at most 3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)). The resulting streams are independent with the correct marginal rates. With independent task marks and queues initially empty, this also bounds total variation of their workload paths on [0,T]. Extending the credited source coupling to stationary starts gives TV<=2*k*r(T)+3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)), where r(T) is the stationary marginal emptying tail. With independent exponential service of rate mu>lambda, a stopped generator calculation gives r(T)<=(1+sqrt(lambda/mu))*exp(-(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2*T). Taking T=2*log(n)/(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2 gives sufficient k=o((n/log(n))^(1/3)). A conditional polynomial tail r(T)<=C*T^(-p) gives sufficient exponent p/(3*p+1). Obstruction: Partial exponential-service sufficient regime only. No optimal threshold, boundary k of order n^(1/3), general-service improvement, correlated-mark result, uniform heavy-traffic result or novelty certification. The basic source coupling is credited. Verification: author_checked_partial. Proof file: proofs/Limited_forkjoin_stationary_exponential_partial.md. (This problem carries 2 attempt records under the same attempt_id; the later, fuller record is reported.)

### P0444. Computational complexity of the multiserver-job stability threshold

**Source.** The Multiserver Job Stochastic Recurrence Equation for Cloud Computing Performance Evaluation (queues_msj_recurrence_2026), Section5; PDF11.

**Statement.** Determine the complexity and certified approximation accuracy of the saturated pile growth rate gamma that defines the FCFS multiserver-job stability threshold. Ledger caveat: The source already establishes the threshold representation lambda_c=1/gamma. A stopped simulation with small successive change is not automatically a certified estimate.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified (Focused later-primary-source checks on 2026-09-07; offline concave scheduling, general FCFS threshold representation, SEK-SMOD and fork-join asymptotics credited. No present-openness certification.). Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison. Result: For the special case where every job needs b servers, put c=floor(s/b). The saturated system is a c-machine list schedule. Its maximum completion time after n jobs is at least total service/c and at most total service/c+(1-1/c)*max_{j<=n}S_j. For iid finite-mean service, total service/n->E[S] and max S_j/n->0 almost surely, so gamma=E[S]/c. Heterogeneous demands break this scalar packing reduction. In the general estimator, a small difference between consecutive sample means does not bound the distance from their limiting value. Obstruction: No general finite-sample certificate or computational complexity bound is derived; the equal-demand case is a credited classical scheduling reduction. Verification: author_checked_partial. No proof file recorded.

### P0451. Unimodularity and reversibility of the Erlang branching spine

**Source.** Moharrami, Subramanian, Liu and Sundaresan: The Erlang Weighted Tree, A New Branching Process (v5, 27 May 2023) (erlang_weighted_tree_2023), Section4, question2; PDF16.

**Statement.** Characterize the relationship between unimodularity of the marked branching tree and reversibility of its source-defined continuous-state spine kernel. Ledger caveat: The reversibility of this particular kernel is already established in the source. The open target is the general relationship and correct change of root, not another proof of detailed balance.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified. Status search: 2026-09-07 bounded primary searches for EWT, La-Kabkab and bilateral preference degree results; 2025 connectivity theorem credited. No current-open or novelty certification. Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Exact conditioning, spectral integral estimate, deterministic graph comparison or order-statistic asymptotics. Result: For the displayed kernel p(x,y)=min(x,y)*g2(y)*f0(y)/(beta0*f0(x)), the measure with density pi(x)=g2(x)*f0(x)^2 has symmetric pair flow pi(x)p(x,y)=min(x,y)*g2(x)*g2(y)*f0(x)*f0(y)/beta0. This recovers the credited reversibility by inspection. The obstacle to identifying it with ordinary unimodular rerooting is the reproductive f0 bias: unimodularity is a mass-transport identity for the root law, while the spine favors descendants through the right eigenfunction. One must construct and normalize a two-sided marked spine with the appropriate Radon-Nikodym factor before claiming an equivalence. Obstruction: No general equivalence, converse, or root-bias formula beyond this explicit kernel calculation is proved. Verification: author_checked_partial. No proof file recorded.

Result: The local-limit argument controls the fraction of vertices in components above a fixed size; it does not put those vertices in one component. To break that inference, compare one cycle of size n with a disjoint union of cycles of length floor(sqrt(n)), adjusting a negligible remainder. Both local weak limits are the bi-infinite path, which is infinite with probability one. The largest component fractions instead tend to one and zero. ### P0453. Weaker degree-tail hypotheses for Erlang weighted-tree growth

**Source.** Moharrami, Subramanian, Liu and Sundaresan: The Erlang Weighted Tree, A New Branching Process (v5, 27 May 2023) (erlang_weighted_tree_2023), Section4, question4; PDF16; Section5.4.

**Our work.** Method: Exact conditioning, spectral integral estimate, deterministic graph comparison or order-statistic asymptotics. Result: One spectral step only needs finite mean. Put g2(x)=exp(-x)*sum_(j>=2)P(j)*x^(j-2)/(j-2)!, and consider Kf(x)=integral min(x,y)*f(y)*g2(y)dy on L2(g2 dx). Tonelli gives integral x*g2(x)dx=sum_(j>=2)(j-1)P(j)=E[K_degree]-1. Since min(x,y)^2<=x*y, the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is at most (E[K_degree]-1)^2. Thus finite mean already makes this symmetric integral operator compact. The kernel is also positive semidefinite because min(x,y)=integral_0^infinity 1_(t<x)*1_(t<y)dt. This removes an exponential moment from the compactness step, while leaving the stronger population conclusions untouched. Obstruction: No assertion that every source growth/extinction theorem survives under finite mean. ### P0461. Entropy concavity for determinantal kernels

**Source.** Lyons: Determinantal probability, basic properties and conjectures, ICM 2014 (lyons_determinantal_2014), Conjectures2.6 and5.3; PDF5,22.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified. Status search: 2026-09-07 bounded primary searches on entropy concavity, union coupling, block factors, Fuglede-Kadison domination and the linear distance bound. **Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact special-case argument and failure analysis after checking the incoming source. Result: The coordinate-diagonal case is a sum of binary entropies, whose second derivatives are -1/[q(1-q)]. There is also an explicit non-diagonal line: for Q(c)=[[1/2,c],[c,1/2]], |c|<1/2, the empty and doubleton probabilities are a=1/4-c^2 and the two singleton probabilities are b=1/4+c^2. Hence H(c)=-2*a*log(a)-2*b*log(b), and Hsecond(c)=4*log(a/b)-8*c^2*(1/a+1/b)<=0. Continuity includes c=+-1/2. This verifies concavity on this affine kernel line. In general the determinant probabilities depend nonlinearly on Q, so concavity of Shannon entropy in a probability vector cannot be applied directly to an arithmetic kernel midpoint. **Statement.** For a trigonometric polynomial f:T->[0,1] of degree m, is its stationary determinantal process an (m+1)-block factor of iid variables? Ledger caveat: The source credits Broman2005 for degree one. A sublattice reduction proves new cases only when the lower-degree process already has a suitable block-factor construction; it is not an induction proving every even degree.

**Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact special-case argument and failure analysis after checking the incoming source. Result: Let f(theta)=g(k*theta). Its Fourier coefficients vanish at lags not divisible by k, so the determinantal kernel is block diagonal on the k residue classes. Determinant factorization proves that these restrictions are independent copies of P_g. If P_g can be represented as F(U_j,...,U_(j+r)) with iid U, define Y_i=F(U_i,U_(i+k),...,U_(i+r*k)). This is a shift-equivariant function of the window U_i,...,U_(i+r*k), so is an (r*k+1)-block factor. The residue-class families use disjoint iid coordinates and have the correct laws. In particular any single-harmonic symbol a+b*cos(k*theta)+c*sin(k*theta) with range in [0,1] inherits the known degree-one construction and is a (k+1)-block factor. Obstruction: General mixed-harmonic symbols remain untreated. Finite dependence by itself does not imply a block-factor representation. Verification: author_checked_restricted_argument. ### P0464. Geometric-mean product bounds for equivariant determinantal laws

**Source.** Lyons: Determinantal probability, basic properties and conjectures, ICM 2014 (lyons_determinantal_2014), Conjecture5.7; PDF23.

**Statement.** For a Gamma-equivariant positive contraction Q on l2(Gamma), establish or refute the optimal stochastic product bounds with lower density FK(Q)=exp(tr log Q) and upper density 1-FK(I-Q). Ledger caveat: The following classical conditioning argument gives weaker harmonic-mean bounds for finite groups and 0<Q<I. It is an author-checked supporting calculation, not a novelty claim or a solution of the geometric-mean conjecture.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified. Status search: 2026-09-07 bounded primary searches on entropy concavity, union coupling, block factors, Fuglede-Kadison domination and the linear distance bound. Known rank-one coupling and degree-one block-factor cases credited. No current-openness certificate. Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact special-case argument and failure analysis after checking the incoming source. Result: Put J=Q(I-Q)^(-1). Given the occupied set B outside e, the conditional odds of presence are s_B=J_ee-J_eB*(J_BB)^(-1)*J_Be. Schur-complement minimization makes s_B decrease as B increases. Its minimum is s_all=1/(J^(-1))ee=1/[(Q^(-1))ee-1]. The conditional probability, however, is s_all/(1+s_all)=1/(Q^(-1))ee. Equivariance makes (Q^(-1))ee=tr(Q^(-1)), with normalized trace, so this probability is the harmonic mean h of all eigenvalues counted with multiplicity. Sequential sampling with common independent uniforms couples the process above iid Bernoulli(h), since every conditional probability given a partial reveal is also at least h. Applying the same argument to the complement gives the upper density 1-HM(I-Q). AM-GM applied to the reciprocals gives HM(Q)<=FK(Q), exposing the exact remaining gap. Obstruction: No geometric-mean domination theorem or sharpness certificate. Numerical coupling feasibility is not exact proof, and the infinite-group extension of this particular calculation is not asserted. Verification: author_checked_restricted_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0465. Linear coupling distance for noncommuting equivariant kernels

**Source.** Lyons: Determinantal probability, basic properties and conjectures, ICM 2014 (lyons_determinantal_2014), Section5.2 afterTheorem5.6; PDF23.

**Statement.** For sofic-group equivariant positive contractions Q,Qprime, does the invariant normalized Hamming coupling distance satisfy dbar(P_Q,P_Qprime)<=||Q-Qprime||_1 without a commutativity assumption? Ledger caveat: The source states the linear bound for commuting pairs and a weaker power bound in general. We examine why the natural common-upper-kernel proof fails; the example is not a counterexample to the actual coupling inequality.

**Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact special-case argument and failure analysis after checking the incoming source. Result: Write D=Q-Qprime. A tempting common upper kernel is R=Qprime+Dplus=(Q+Qprime+|D|)/2. It dominates both in operator order, but need not be a contraction. In dimension two take Q=diag(1,0) and Qprime=(1/2)*[[1,1],[1,1]]. Then D^2=I/2 and |D|=I/sqrt(2). The largest eigenvalue of Q+Qprime is 1+1/sqrt(2), giving lambda_max(R)=1/2+1/sqrt(2)>1. Thus R is not an admissible determinantal kernel and one cannot apply monotone-coupling bounds through it. This same obstruction can be placed in the two-dimensional irreducible block of the right group algebra of S3, with zeros on the other blocks; the resulting operators commute with left translations but not with one another. Obstruction: Failure of a common-upper-kernel construction does not refute the desired distance inequality. No claim of having executed a nonabelian coupling LP. Result: Conditional on Z, the extremal leaders form a Poisson process with intensity Z(dx)*exp(-alpha*h)dh. Thus the probability that all heights are at most t is exp(-Z(D)*exp(-alpha*t)/alpha), and the joint maximum density measure is exp(-alpha*t)*E[Z(dx)*exp(-Z(D)*exp(-alpha*t)/alpha)]dt, matching equation12.86. Integrating over t gives the position marginal E[Z(dx)/Z(D)]. This is well-defined although E[Z(D)] is infinite under the source critical-tail law. ### P0482. Ballisticity and an absolutely continuous stationary environment law

**Source.** Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment (drewitz_ramirez_rwre_2014), Open question2.19 PDF24; Corollary2.15 PDF20-21.

**Statement.** Under stationary ergodicity and ellipticity, does directional ballisticity imply an invariant probability law for the environment viewed from the particle that is absolutely continuous with respect to the environment law? Ledger caveat: The opposite implication, assuming directional transience, is already Corollary2.15 of the source. Its stationary-increment recurrence argument supplies strict positive speed; this is not an unresolved part of the target.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified. Status search: Bounded2026-09-07 primary searches and archived later theorems checked. No current-openness certificate; known stationary/non-nestling/homogeneous cases credited. Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact restricted argument and corrected proof-obstruction analysis. Result: Let R be the environment transition kernel. Every P*R^i is absolutely continuous with respect to the translation-invariant P. Its density is the finite sum f_i(omega)=sum_x P_(-x),omega[X_i=0], obtained by changing variables under a spatial shift in the annealed endpoint formula. Set g_n=(1/n)*sum_(i=0)^(n-1) f_i. If these densities are uniformly integrable in L1(P), Dunford-Pettis gives a weak-L1 convergent subsequence g_n to g, with g>=0 and integral g=1. For bounded measurable h, integral(Rh-h)*g_n dP=((P*R^n)h-P h)/n tends to zero. Weak-L1 convergence passes both bounded test functions, so g dP is invariant. A uniform Lp bound for some p>1 would suffice, since integral_(g_n>K) g_n<=K^(1-p)*integral g_n^p. This isolates an explicit missing estimate: positive speed must supply enough control of these occupation densities, not merely weak compactness of the environment space. Obstruction: No density-uniform-integrability estimate follows here from ballisticity. The invariant-law-to-positive-speed direction is credited to the source; no unsupported assertion that iid regeneration alone always gives a full-space absolutely continuous invariant law. Verification: author_checked_restricted_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0483. Directional transience versus positive speed under uniform ellipticity

**Source.** Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment (drewitz_ramirez_rwre_2014), Open question2.20 PDF24; renewal identities PDF47-49.

**Statement.** For nearest-neighbor iid uniformly elliptic RWRE on Z^d, d>=2, does transience in direction ell imply positive limiting speed in that direction? Ledger caveat: Equivalence of conditions(T) and(Tprime), proved by Guerra-Ramirez, does not answer this question.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified. Status search: Bounded2026-09-07 primary searches and archived later theorems checked. No current-openness certificate; known stationary/non-nestling/homogeneous cases credited. Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact restricted argument and corrected proof-obstruction analysis. Result: Uniform ellipticity gives a precise finite-trap bound. Suppose every site of a finite set A has a nearest-neighbor path of at most m steps leading outside A, and every transition probability is at least kappa. At each block of m steps before exit, the conditional probability of leaving is at least kappa^m. The strong Markov property yields P_x,omega[tau_A>j*m]<=(1-kappa^m)^j and E_x,omega[tau_A]<=m*kappa^(-m). For A=[-R,R]^d intersect Z^d, m=2R+1 works by moving along one coordinate. Thus no fixed-size trap has an arbitrarily large quenched mean under uniform ellipticity. But the bound grows exponentially with R; it cannot be summed over the random spatial extent explored before regeneration without a further tail estimate. For coordinate directions, the source renewal formula gives positive speed exactly when the conditional mean regeneration time is finite; almost-sure finite regeneration times alone do not supply it. Obstruction: No estimate on the distribution of the size or shape of a regeneration excursion, and no proof that transience implies an integrable regeneration time. Verification: author_checked_restricted_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0485. Transience of elliptic iid environments in dimension at least three

**Source.** Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment (drewitz_ramirez_rwre_2014), Open question2.23 PDF25.

**Statement.** Is every nearest-neighbor elliptic iid random walk in random environment on Z^d transient when d>=3? Ledger caveat: Transience means finitely many visits to each site, not transience in a specified direction. The following homogeneous calculation is a classical special case.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified. Status search: Bounded2026-09-07 primary searches and archived later theorems checked. No current-openness certificate; known stationary/non-nestling/homogeneous cases credited. Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact restricted argument and corrected proof-obstruction analysis. Result: For a deterministic homogeneous elliptic environment, the increments are iid. Nonzero mean gives transience by the strong law. If the mean is zero, nearest-neighbor steps force p(e_i)=p(-e_i)>0 for every i. The characteristic function is phi(t)=2*sum_i p(e_i)*cos(t_i). Its absolute value equals1 only at the two torus points with all coordinates0 or all coordinates pi. Taylor expansion at each gives |phi(t)|<=1-c*dist(t,S)^2 locally, while compactness bounds it strictly below1 elsewhere. Fourier inversion therefore bounds the return probability by C*n^(-d/2). The sum over n is finite for d>=3, proving transience through the expected visit count. For a spatially varying environment the quenched increments are no longer iid and there is no one fixed characteristic function whose nth power gives the transition law. Obstruction: No heat-kernel estimate for general iid elliptic environments. A central limit theorem by itself is not a local return-probability bound. Verification: author_checked_restricted_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0486. Directional zero-one law beyond the plane

**Source.** Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment (drewitz_ramirez_rwre_2014), Open question3.2 PDF42.

**Statement.** For elliptic iid nearest-neighbor RWRE on Z^d, d>=3, prove or disprove P_0[A_ell] in{0,1} for every direction ell. Ledger caveat: A_ell and A_minusell are disjoint by definition. Showing their intersection is empty proves no zero-one law. The source credits the dimension-two theorem to Zerner-Merkl.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified. Status search: Bounded2026-09-07 primary searches and archived later theorems checked. No current-openness certificate; known stationary/non-nestling/homogeneous cases credited. Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact restricted argument and corrected proof-obstruction analysis. Result: There is a useful stationary-measure special case. Suppose additionally that the environment process has an invariant probability Q absolutely continuous with respect to P. Kozlov gives Q equivalent to P. Put q(omega)=P_0,omega[A_ell]. By the Markov property and invariance of A_ell under deleting finitely many steps, q(eta_n)=E[1_Aell|omega,X_0,...,X_n] is a bounded martingale and tends to1_Aell. Under initial law Q the variables q(eta_n) all have the same distribution, so q(eta_0) itself must take values only0 and1. The harmonic identity q(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)*q(t_e omega), together with ellipticity, then forces every neighboring shift to have the same value on a common full-measure set. Spatial ergodicity of P makes q constant, establishing the directional zero-one law in this restricted class. The absent invariant law is the obstruction to applying this stationary argument to all iid environments. Obstruction: No existence proof for Q in a general elliptic iid environment. The argument is a credited stationary special-case rederivation, not a solution of the higher-dimensional question. Verification: author_checked_restricted_argument. No proof file recorded.

### P0487. Does positive velocity force a quantitative ballisticity condition?

**Source.** Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment (drewitz_ramirez_rwre_2014), Open question3.20 PDF52; Theorem3.17 PDF51.

**Statement.** Under iid uniform ellipticity, does positive velocity in direction ell imply the polynomial ballisticity condition(P)_M for M>15d+5? Ledger caveat: The source links stretched-exponential slab conditions to exponential moments of the spatial regeneration radius, not to an asserted equivalence with arbitrary time moments.

**Status.** Historical status: source_says_open. Current-literature status: unverified. Status search: Bounded2026-09-07 primary searches and archived later theorems checked. No current-openness certificate; known stationary/non-nestling/homogeneous cases credited. Admission: admitted; result_status: unsolved.

**Our work.** Method: Integrator-authored exact restricted argument and corrected proof-obstruction analysis. Result: For the known non-nestling subcase with local projected drift at least delta>0 everywhere, let xi be a one-step displacement in direction ell. Since |xi|<=1, E[exp(-a*xi)|past]<=1-a*delta+a^2*exp(a)/2. Choosing0<a<=min(1,delta/exp(1)) makes exp(-a*X_n dot ell) a nonnegative supermartingale. Stopping at a backward level-bL gives probability at most exp(-a*bL) of ever reaching it. Nearby directions retain a positive drift lower bound, giving the slab decay needed for(T), and hence the known polynomial condition. Positive limiting velocity alone supplies no such uniform local drift. Even at the level of abstract regeneration times, finite first moment gives only n*P[T>n]->0: the valid tail P[T>n]=1/((n+1)*log(n+exp(1))^2), n>=0, has finite mean and no moment1+epsilon. This is an implication counterdiagnostic, not a RWRE construction or a claimed equivalence between slab exits and time moments. Obstruction: No self-improvement from positive velocity to the required exit bound in the nestling case, and no counterexample satisfying iid uniform ellipticity. Verification: author_checked_restricted_argument. No proof file recorded.

### C0001. Joint scaling limit of all intermediate level sets of the 2D DGFF

Source: Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes (`biskup_dgff_extrema_2020`), Problem 16.1, p. 220.

Statement: Extract a joint distributional limit of the level sets {x in D_N : h_x >= 2 sqrt(g) lambda log N} (or the point measures (2.29)) simultaneously for all lambda in (0,1); couple the limit measures Z^D_lambda and show they all arise via the LQG construction from one underlying continuum GFF.

Status: historical status source_says_open; current-literature status unverified.

Our work (attempt C0001-A001). Method: Reduce to tightness plus a characterisation of subsequential limits through the Gibbs-Markov property, uniformly in lambda; try to replace the moment method of Theorem 2.7 by a single martingale approximation of the exponential of a Gaussian field. Result: Partial reduction only. For any finite set of lambdas the vector of point measures is tight (each coordinate is), and any subsequential limit satisfies the Gibbs-Markov property coordinatewise; the coupling question is therefore whether the joint limit is the image of one CGFF under the map lambda -> e^{alpha lambda h} dx with the Seneta-Heyde normalisation. Obstruction: Second moments of Z^D_lambda blow up as lambda -> 1/sqrt2 in the moment method; the uniform-in-lambda control needed for a joint limit up to lambda -> 1 is not available from moment calculations. Verification level: unreviewed.

### C0002. Fluctuations and large deviations of intermediate level sets of the 2D DGFF

Source: Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes (`biskup_dgff_extrema_2020`), Problem 16.2, p. 220.

Statement: Describe the rate of convergence in Corollary 2.9 (size of the intermediate level set), identify the limit law of the fluctuations of the level set around its limit, and study deviations whose probability tends to zero as N -> infinity.

Status: historical status source_says_open; current-literature status unverified.

Our work (attempt C0002-A002, correcting C0002-A001). Correction: Codex review 10:53: the Gaussian tail carries a 1/sqrt(log N) factor. Result: CORRECTION of C0002-A001. With Var h_x = g log N + O(1) and threshold 2 sqrt(g) lambda log N, P(h_x >= threshold) = exp(-2 lambda^2 log N)/(sqrt(2 pi) 2 lambda sqrt(log N)) (1 + o(1)), so the mean size of the intermediate level set is of order N^{2 - 2 lambda^2}/sqrt(log N), not a constant times N^{2(1 - lambda^2)} as A001 wrote; the (log N)^{-1/2} is the leading normalisation, not a correction term. Obstruction: No local limit theorem for pairs at every mesoscopic distance uniformly; the fluctuation law is a functional of the whole scale ladder, not of one scale. (carried over from C0002-A001, unchanged by the correction) Independent check: Correction checked line by line against the source and the holder's message by the Fable agent; the holder's claim was taken as a lead, not as authority. Verification level: unreviewed.

### C0003. Bypassing the Laplace-transform tail condition for the DGFF extremal measure

Source: Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes (`biskup_dgff_extrema_2020`), Conjecture 16.3, p. 220.

Statement: Prove that any family of non-trivial random measures {Z^D : D in the class of admissible domains} obeying properties (1)-(4) of Theorem 10.15 (Gibbs-Markov, conformal covariance, positivity, non-atomicity) automatically satisfies property (5), the Laplace-transform tail asymptotics, for some c hat > 0.

Status: historical status source_says_open; current-literature status unverified.

Our work (attempt C0003-A001). Method: Try to derive the tail exponent from the Gibbs-Markov fixed-point equation as for smoothing transforms (Durrett-Liggett classification). Result: The Gibbs-Markov property along dyadic square partitions gives a fixed-point equation of smoothing type Z^D =_d sum_i e^{alpha Phi_i} Z^{D_i} with Gaussian binding field Phi and 4 pieces; Durrett-Liggett gives, for such equations, that non-trivial solutions have tails whose exponent is the root of a structure equation, here forcing E[Z^D(A)^s] finite iff s < 1. This yields the correct tail EXPONENT (P(Z^D(A) > t) decays like t^{-1} up to slowly varying factors) but not the precise Laplace asymptotic E e^{-lambda Z} = 1 - c lambda log(1/lambda)(1+o(1)) demanded by property (5); the slowly varying factor is exactly the content of the conjecture and the Durrett-Liggett theory does not fix it. Obstruction: Smoothing-transform theory fixes the power in the tail but not the logarithmic correction; the log factor is what (5) asserts. Verification level: unreviewed.

### C0005. Size of deep extremal level sets of the 2D DGFF converges to the extremal measure

Source: Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes (`biskup_dgff_extrema_2020`), Conjecture 16.5, p. 221.

Statement: There is c in (0,infinity) such that for each open A in D with Leb(dA)=0, (1/t) e^{-alpha t} #{x in Gamma^D_N(t) : x/N in A} converges in law, as N -> infinity then t -> infinity, to c Z^D(A), jointly for finitely many disjoint open sets.

Status: historical status source_says_open; current-literature status unverified.

Our work (attempt C0005-A001). Method: Use the cluster-process structure (Theorem 9.2) to write the level-set count as a sum over local maxima of cluster sizes, then a law of large numbers over clusters. Result: Gamma_N(A,t) = sum over extremal local maxima in A below depth t of the cluster size at depth t - (gap). Given Z^D, the maxima form a Poisson process with intensity Z^D(dx) e^{-alpha h} dh and the clusters are i.i.d.; the expected total is Z^D(A) integral_0^t e^{alpha s} E[cluster size at depth s] ds. Obstruction: Uniform-in-N control of the deep-cluster size at depth t (order t e^{alpha t} by Seneta-Heyde) is not available from the concentric decomposition beyond bounded depth. Verification level: unreviewed.

Our work (attempt C0006-A001). Method: Renewal-type argument on the cluster process viewed from the local maximum: depth-h count as a branching-like functional of the concentric decomposition. Result: Writing the cluster as the field pinned at a local maximum, e^{-alpha h} E nu(f_h) is the expected number of points at depth h weighted by e^{-alpha h}; the concentric decomposition expresses the cluster as a random walk with a Bessel-like entropic repulsion plus independent fine fields, so f_h is a sum over scales k <= log(h) of contributions, each of order e^{alpha h} times the probability that the walk is at height h at scale k. Obstruction: Scale inhomogeneity of the concentric-decomposition walk defeats the standard renewal theorem. Verification level: unreviewed.
